idiom_name: trait port + adapter struct + newtype conversions (From/TryFrom) behind module privacy
implementation_notes: Rust expresses the boundary as a trait the domain owns (pub trait OrderPort { fn place(&self, order: &Order) -> Result<Receipt, Rejected>; }) plus an adapter struct in a module that is the only one depending on the vendor crate; foreign values are converted at the edge with newtypes and From/TryFrom - infallible, meaning-preserving conversions in From, anything that can reject in TryFrom with a typed error - while serde or the vendor's own parser owns only the wire half. What replaces the facade/adapter/translator trio is the trait, the newtype and the TryFrom impl; an explicit adapter type is still justified when the upstream client needs state, pooling or retries. Module privacy plus pub(crate)/pub use is what keeps vendor types out of the domain.
pitfalls: Implementing From with validation inside (or unwrap-ing) hides a fallible conversion behind .into(); fallible seams belong in TryFrom returning a typed error.
The orphan rule forces a local wrapper for a foreign trait: a newtype keeps From/TryFrom implementable, but a public inner field defeats it.
Option in the vendor payload must be mapped deliberately (Option vs default), and #[serde(default)] versus deny_unknown_fields encodes the tolerance policy.
There is no runtime reflection across the boundary: a payload field that no longer deserialises fails at parse time, so let the DTO absorb upstream additions rather than tightening the domain type.
